title: 5 USC 552(a)(1,2) documents

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Request: 5 USC 552(a)(1,2) documents
communications.communication:
Dear FOIA department:

This is a FOIA request for all records described by 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(1, 2), as well as processing records for this request itself.

In particular, I request:

1. All:

a) descriptions of its central and field organization and the established places at which, the employees (and in the case of a uniformed service, the members) from whom, and the methods whereby, the public may obtain information, make submittals or requests, or obtain decisions;
b) statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined, including the nature and requirements of all formal and informal procedures available;
c) rules of procedure, descriptions of forms available or the places at which forms may be obtained, and instructions as to the scope and contents of all papers, reports, or examinations;
d) substantive rules of general applicability adopted as authorized by law, and statements of general policy or interpretations of general applicability formulated and adopted by the agency; and
e) each amendment, revision, or repeal of the foregoing.

… except that you may, at your discretion, exclude records published in the Federal Register.

2. All:
a) final opinions, including concurring and dissenting opinions, as well as orders, made in the adjudication of cases;
b) those statements of policy and interpretations which have been adopted by the agency;
c) administrative staff manuals and instructions to staff that affect a member of the public;
d) copies of all records, regardless of form or format that have been requested 3 or more times; and
e) a general index of the records referred to under subparagraph (D); and
f) current indexes providing identifying information for the public as to any matter issued, adopted, or promulgated after July 4, 1967, and identified in paragraphs (A)-(E)

… except  that you may, at your discretion, exclude records published in the Federal Register, or available on your online FOIA reading room.



For the purposes of this request, all terms above have the same meaning as they do in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(1, 2).



I also request:
3. all records relating to the fulfillment of this request

This part of the request is to be processed only AFTER you have completed processing all of the above parts. Do not conduct any search for records under this part earlier than that.

This part does not request that you create any new record; rather, it requests the records that you will have created in processing the above parts, and will therefore exist before you conduct the search for this part. See McGehee v. CIA, 697 F. 2d 1095, 1100-05 (D.C. Cir. 1983) (agency must use time-of-search cut-off date, not time-of-request).


For all responsive records, I also request:

1. all parts of the record (i.e. no portion of a record with some responsive portion may be considered "non-responsive");
2. all versions of the record, whether or not currently in use;
3. all record metadata, such as dates on which they were drafted, passed, went into effect, withdrawn, or similar events; person(s) / office(s) responsible; authors;  IDs; revision numbers; etc.;
4. a detailed index of all claims of exemption/privilege, regardless of whether the record is claimed to be exempt in whole or in part;
5. access to inspect the record directly, in its native electronic format; and
6. if any classification applies, mandatory declassification review (MDR) under E.O. 13526, and the result of the MDR, including any declassified records.

For all requests above, the "cut-off date" is, at the earliest, the date that you conduct the search.


Please note that this request is made after the enactment of Public Law No. 114-185, S. 337 (114th), the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 (FOIA IA). The revised statute, as specified in the FOIA IA, applies to this request. FOIA IA § 6. In particular, please note that:

1. you must provide electronic format documents, §§ 552(a)(2) (undesignated preceding text), 552(a)(2)(E) (undesignated following text), 552(a)(3)(B), and 552(a)(3)(C);
2. you may not specify an appeal duration less than 90 days, § 552(a)(6)(C)(A)(i)(III)(aa);
3. you may not withhold any record unless "the agency reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption described in subsection (b), or disclosure is prohibited by law", § 552(a)(8)(A)(i);
4. you must segregate and partially release records where possible, §§ 552(a)(8)(A)(ii) and 552(b) (undesignated matter following (b)(9)); and
5. you may not claim deliberative process exemption for records more than 25 years old, § 552(b)(5).


This request specifically excludes providing me with new copies of any records which have been already provided to me or published online for free (e.g. on the agency's online "reading room"), in full or identically to the form that would be provided to me under this request (i.e. with exactly the same format, redactions, and claimed exemptions).

This is only an exclusion on providing records under this request that are identical to those already provided to me or available online, and only if I am or have already been provided a link to the online version (if "available online").

This exclusion is only intended to limit unnecessary duplication or provision, not to limit what records are responsive to this request, nor to permit failure to disclose the location of a responsive record available online. If this exclusion would in any way increase the cost or duration to respond to this request, it is to be ignored to the extent it does so.


This request is to be treated as separate from all others that I have filed.


Please forward this request to the FOIA office of every agency component and subcomponent that may have responsive records for independent processing, with a copy to me.

This request includes any records held jointly by your agency in conjunction with any other agency and/or department, in interagency and/or interdepartmental systems of records, or by other agencies or third parties (including contractors) acting pursuant any agreement with your agency.


With the possible exception of the index of records claimed to be exempt or privileged, this request does not ask you to create new records. If you determine that a response would require creating a new record that you do not want to create, please first contact me by email with an explanation of what records you have that would most closely match the information requested and might be acceptable substitutes, so that we can reasonably tailor the request.

In particular, I specifically request that you do not create new documents in response to this request that are modifications of a digital record, such as page-view images, print views, scans, or the like. No such creation or substitution is authorized by FOIA or the Privacy Act.

However, if the same or similar records are held in both electronic and paper formats, this request includes both the paper and electronic versions. The paper version and the digital version are distinct records, and each may contain distinct information such as handwritten or other markings on the paper copy and embedded metadata in the electronic version.

Furthermore, to the extent that the native electronic format is proprietary or otherwise not in format accessible by widely available, open source software, I request that you also provide an export of the proprietary format into a standard, open format, as described below.


Please note that the FOIA requires you to service the maximum extent of my request that can be done via e.g. partial redaction of exempt material. If you believe some portions of a record to be exempt because it contains Sensitive Security Information (SSI,  49 CFR 15, 1520) or classified information (18 USC 798), please provide a version of the record redacted to the minimum extent necessary to remove exempt information (e.g. per  49 CFR 1520.15), along with adequate information to describe the reason for each specific exemption.


In order to help tailor my request, please provide an upfront estimate of the time and cost it will take to complete this request, broken down any significant factors that would affect cost to service, number of records in each category, and your estimate of how many records in the category are likely to be exempt.


Please provide me with incremental updates, with updated estimates for fulfillment of the remainder, rather than having the entirety of the request be blocked until fully completed.


In accordance with 5 USC 552(a)(3)(B, C) (E-FOIA), Rehabilitation Act § 508, and FOIA IA, please respond using native format, electronic, machine-processable, accessible, open, and well structured records to the maximum extent possible. This means, e.g.:

* native format records rather than PDFs or other conversions (note above re providing both native electronic records and scans of paper records, if both exist);
* individual files per distinct source record (e.g. one .msg file per email), named clearly using the record's identifier, title, and date, rather than a single file containing multiple concatenated records;
* records compliant with the Rehabilitation Act § 508, 36 CFR 1194.22, USAB ATBCB-2015-0002, and I​SO 14289­-1;
* fully digital text records rather than scans, rasterizations, or OCR;
* complete electronic records, as held on any computer (including phones, servers, backup servers, mail servers, workstations, etc.), including all headers and attachments, fully expanded e-mail addresses, full addresses for address "aliases", full lists for "distribution list" aliases, all embedded and external metadata, complete bitwise digital copies of the original file, all file headers, and all other file content;
* blackout rather than whiteout redactions, with every redaction marked with all exemption(s) claimed for that redaction;
* digital redactions rather than black marker or rasterization;
* lists and structured data as machine-processable spreadsheets (e.g. CSV, SQL, XSL) rather than word documents (e.g. DOC, PDF, TXT, RTF) or partial printouts (e.g. PDF);
* open format records (e.g. PDF, AVI, MPG) rather than proprietary format records (e.g. WordPerfect, Microsoft Advanced Systems Format (ASF)) (note above re providing both original, proprietary format records and open format records);
* scans rather than paper copies;
* digital audio/video files rather than physical tapes;
* upload to your Electronic Reading Room (or other publicly accessible server) rather than personal transfer (for all items other than the item requesting records related to me or my requests);
* email or (S)FTP file transfer rather than CD;
* email correspondence rather than physical mail; etc.

Multiple files may be sent in a combined, compressed form using standard ZIP, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, and/or RAR formats, or sent as separate files, at your discretion.

However, do not use a password on any files, including ZIP files etc. If a password was present in the native format, leave it unaltered, send me the password.


If there are any files you prefer not to transfer by email (e.g. if they are more than 10MB), please upload them to me via the link listed below my signature.

Doing so is secure, completely free to you, and the files uploaded will go to me directly.


Please note that this request does not request that you physically "duplicate" records, as I do not want you to create any paper or other physical copy for me — I only want electronic versions (or scans, for records that are not fully available in electronic form). As such, I expect there to be no duplication related costs.

Furthermore, I specifically request access for inspection of the records, including direct electronic access, in native format, to any electronic records.


I am not currently willing to pay for servicing this request. I may be willing to pay if it is necessary; please send a detailed explanation of the costs and their statutory justification, and service the maximum extent of the request that can be done for free in the meantime.

I request that, pending fee waiver determination or appeal, you proceed with this request as if it were in the "other non-commercial requester" category.

This request is a qualified request for journalistic, public interest purposes (entitling me to fully waived fees). As such, I request public interest fee waiver and journalistic fee waiver.

1. I have no commercial interest in these records.

2. I am a representative of the news media and entitled to waiver of all search fees.

I intend and am able to host and publish all received records online to the general public at no charge, as well to publish highlights, analyses, summaries, commentaries, and other creative, original journalistic work about responsive records through multiple online publications, such as https://plus.google.com/+saizai, https://twitter.com/saizai, and https://s.ai/foia (among others).

I also have a standing agreement with BoingBoing to publish articles about these matters, under my byline, on boingboing.net.

I have previously made journalistic publication, extraction, commentary, and analysis based on my FOIA/PA requests, e.g. relating to TSA, DHS, DOJ, and USPS activities, which have gotten widespread public interest, attention, and comment, and resulted in secondary journalistic publications based on my original work. This includes publications such as The New York Times, Forbes, Bloomberg/BNA, ABC News/Fusion, RT America News, RightThisMinute, and BoingBoing. I intend to do the same with this request.

3. The records are of significant public interest, entitled to waiver of all duplication fees, since

a) as above, I both am able and intend to disseminate the files widely;
b) they would contribute greatly to the public understanding of the operations and activities of your agency, in that they are records that directly describe agency operations and activities, as well as the issues and matters described at the top of this letter;
c) they are not currently readily available;
d) their existence constitutes prima facie evidence of your agency's violation of Congress' explicit command in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(1, 2) that your agency publish all the primary requested records; and
e) Congress has statutorily mandated that they be published freely, i.e. made a statutory finding that they are records of such significant public interest that they must be published without any request.

4. As mentioned above, I am explicitly not asking for any physical duplication, but rather direct server-to-server file transfer or email (or posting on your website). The FOIA authorizes duplication fees strictly limited to your agency's actual costs, and mandates that your agency use the cheapest available requested methods. I consider the actual costs for server-to-server file transfer to be reasonably estimated by, e.g., Amazon S3's pricing (https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/).


If you have any questions or updates about this request, please contact me by email.

Please ensure that all of your responses comply with § 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, 36 CFR 1194.22, and UESB NPRM ATBCB-2015-0002.

In particular, please make all correspondence pursuant to this request — including notification and responsive records — by email, with native electronic format records, as specified in the request. I do not authorize you to send anything to me by physical mail unless I specifically state otherwise.

My email address is sufficient for all response to this request, and I can provide you with free means of electronic transfer for records too large to email.

Do not respond using ZixCorp "Secure Mail" or any other method that "expires" records from being available. Use only actual email and direct attachments, unless I explicitly request otherwise.


Please let me know your tracking number(s) for this request upon receipt, as well as your specific estimated completion date. 5 USC 552(a)(7).

If you believe that any of the requested items are not reasonably described, or that you need any further information regarding my qualification for fee waivers, please be specific about what you consider vague and what questions I can answer that would clarify them.

This request is made via MuckRock. You may provide responsive records either directly to me (see below my sig), or via MuckRock, as described below.

Sincerely,
Sai				(Note: Sai is my full legal name; I am mononymic.)
President, SaiCorp, Inc.
SaiCorp is an organization devoted to public interest journalism, government transparency and accountability, individuals' civil rights, and related issues.

NOTE: This request is made on behalf of both myself, Sai (in personal capacity) and SaiCorp, Inc. (in official capacity).

Phone: +1 510 394 4724  (please leave voicemail if I do not pick up)
Email: foia@saizai.com
Upload link: https://www.dropbox.com/request/kbR4D5SjIrVxm1eE4uHn
Other identifiers for search purposes: "Sai", "saizai", "SaiCorp", "saizai.com", "s.ai", "i@s.ai", "legal@s.ai", "dccc@s.ai", "foia@saizai.com", "tsa@saizai.com", "saizai@gmail.com"
Physical mail: 500 Westover Dr. #4514, Sanford, NC 27330

NOTE: Do not physically mail responsive records without my explicit request. Send all records in native electronic form, as described above.

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #F17-00085
communications.communication:
Dear OPR -

1. Your response to part 1 of my request does not address the terms of the request. It specifically is directed at 552(a)(1) described records that have NOT been published as required by that statute.

Please provide all such records. If there are no responsive records because all records so described ARE published, then please respond by saying so.

2. You did not address part 2(e) of my request, which requires an "index" of (2)(d) records.

3. The form format of the records you provided does not match what was requested: native, electronic, § 508 accessible, separate files per source file, with metadata intact, etc. etc. as specifically described in the request.

What you provided is concatenated, rasterized scans, which my request explicitly calls out as not acceptable.

Please provide the records in the form and format requested.

Sincerely,
Sai

On September 27, 2017, our office released records to you in response to your FOIA request.  At that time, you were provided with information regarding your right to file an administrative appeal.  Please be advised that the statutory timeframe for filing an appeal has expired.  An appeal was required to be submitted within 90 business days of the date of our response.  Accordingly, FOIA Request F17-00085 has been properly closed.

If you are seeking additional records, you may submit a new FOIA request.

Thank you,

OPR FOIA
(202) 514-3365
OPR.FOIA@usdoj.gov

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Public-records request — OCR case 02-22-1153 monitoring records (Jan. 1, 2025–present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Please provide electronic copies of records maintained by PLUMSTED TOWNSHIP SCHOOL DISTRICT from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request concerning the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights (OCR) resolution agreement in OCR case 02-22-1153.

I request the following existing records:

1. District correspondence with OCR about the identified agreement or case, including messages to or from OCR-Transition@ed.gov, the OCR staff addresses identified in the Agreement or Letter, and other Department of Education addresses ending in @ed.gov when the message concerns this case, agreement, or a related monitoring submission. This includes OCR acknowledgments, feedback, approvals, requests for revision or additional information, closure-related messages, and any bounced, undeliverable, rejected, failed-delivery, out-of-office, automated-reply, non-delivery, or other delivery-status messages, as well as follow-up messages or internal records indicating that an attempted OCR contact or submission did not receive a response. Include attachments and transmittal emails.
2. Records submitted, prepared for submission, or maintained for submission to OCR, including reports, data, policies, training materials, remediation records, implementation updates, requests for approval, transmittal emails, and records identifying deliverables, deadlines, or responsible staff.
3. Internal district emails or memoranda about an inability to reach OCR, delivery failures, unacknowledged submissions, unanswered follow-ups, delayed OCR feedback or approval, delayed submission, or delayed agreement work.

If no responsive records exist, please state that explicitly. If any portion is withheld, please identify the specific exemption and release all reasonably segregable portions.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Meredith Kolodner

communications.subject: RE: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Public-records request — OCR case 02-22-1153 monitoring records (Jan. 1, 2025–present)
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Ytreboe,

t's now November 4, and I appreciate your response but it doesn’t meet the requirements of the Open Public Records Act.

Under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), a custodian who is unable to comply with a request “shall indicate the specific basis therefor.” Your response states only " If your request is not responded to by November 4, 2026, it
shall be deemed denied." It does not identify the statute, regulation, executive order, or other authority relied on, and it does not state which of my request items it applies to.

Please provide within five business days a supplemental written response that:

1) addresses each item in my request separately;
2) cites the specific statutory or regulatory exemption for any record withheld in full, and explains why it applies;
under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-5(g), discloses the remainder of any record that is partly exempt, and identifies each redaction and its legal basis;
3) states whether any responsive records exist that you have not located or reviewed; and
identifies any records withheld under a common-law privilege.

I also note that under N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6, the agency bears the burden of proving that a denial of access is authorized by law, and that N.J.S.A. 47:1A-8 preserves my common law right of access to these records. I request that you consider access on that basis as well.


Sincerely,
Meredith Kolodner, The Hechinger Report
917-881-3896

title: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (South Hadley Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (South Hadley Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: ACTION REQUIRED / Alaska DOC public records request / Parole Board
communications.communication:
In the future, to ensure efficient processing, please submit your request through the appropriate portal: https://doc.alaska.gov/public-records-request.
Do not send requests directly to the facility.

Per AS 40.25.122 and 2 AAC 96.220, the Department may ask if a requester is a party or represents a party in an administrative or judicial litigation with the state in which a requested record is relevant. If the answer is YES, the requester must seek the records in accordance with the rules of procedure applicable in the administrative or judicial proceeding.



Please "reply" to this email: Are you such a requestor? (currently in litigation with the state of Alaska)

Yes or no.


It is important to note there may be a cost associated with public records searches, an estimate of which is based on the parameters of your search. Alaska Statute 40.25.110 (c) allows "if the production of records for one requester in a calendar month exceeds five person-hours, the public agency shall require the requester to pay the personnel costs required during the month to complete the search and copying tasks." Additionally, you would need to pay the fee before the records are disclosed. If it is determined this request will exceed five person hours, I can provide you with an estimated cost of the search. Please note that the estimate is for costs associated with searching DOC records and is no guarantee that any responsive records exist. We may not locate any records responsive to your request, and you will still be charged the search fee. If responsive records are located, then those documents allowable for release will be made available to you.



For clarification, please refer to AS 40.25.115 (a) which says, "activities authorized under this section may not take priority over the primary responsibilities of the public agency." Additionally, DOC P&P 108.07 (VII) (B) states "no response shall be sent to a requestor prior to informing and consulting with the Commissioner, Division Director and Department of Law."


Respectfully,
Betsy

title: Public Information Act Request — RFCSP #22-201 Strategic Planning Facilitation: proposals, scoring, negotiation and award records

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Public Information Act Request — RFCSP #22-201 Strategic Planning Facilitation: proposals, scoring, negotiation and award records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Texas Public Information Act (Government Code Chapter 552), I request copies of the following records relating to Richardson Independent School District RFCSP #22-201, "Strategic Planning Facilitation" (released on or about November 2022; proposals due November 28, 2022; awarded to Engage!Learning Inc., also known as engage2learn). The date range for this request is November 1, 2022 through September 30, 2026.

In this request, a reference to any record includes that record under any title the District uses for it; where a title differs, I request the record that serves that function.

1. The complete solicitation document for RFCSP #22-201, including all addenda, the evaluation criteria and weights, and any document stating a budget, estimated cost, or not-to-exceed amount for this procurement.
2. The bid/proposal tabulation (also called a bid abstract, proposal register, or log of proposals received) showing all proposers and all proposed prices, in its native spreadsheet format if maintained as one.
3. All evaluation and scoring records, including: scoring sheets (also called evaluation forms, rating sheets, or scorecards), individual evaluator scores and any consensus or summary scores, scoring rubrics, evaluator comments and worksheets (also called committee notes), and any scores or evaluations from vendor presentations, demonstrations, or interviews. This includes evaluation records and exports maintained in the District's electronic bidding system (Bonfire) or any other e-procurement system.
4. All proposals submitted in response to RFCSP #22-201, including both technical proposals and cost proposals (including any cost proposals submitted under separate cover) from all proposers. If the volume is large, I prioritize: (a) the proposal of Engage!Learning Inc./engage2learn
5. Records and correspondence between the District and the selected proposer regarding price and negotiation, including any best-and-final-offer (BAFO) requests and responses, and any documents showing a revised or negotiated price.
6. The executed contract (also called the agreement or professional services agreement) with the selected proposer, including scope of work, final price, term, and renewal options, plus all amendments, change orders, and extensions.
7. The board agenda item and supporting materials approving this award, including any statement of the funding source (for example, general fund or a grant) and the budgeted amount; if a grant or foundation funded any part of this procurement, the grant agreement or memorandum of understanding; or other records sufficient to identify the funding source and the budgeted amount.
8. Line-item invoices submitted by, and payments (also called payment records or disbursement records) made to, the selected proposer under this contract, from the contract start through September 30, 2026.
9. The final deliverable(s) (also called work products or final reports) produced under this contract, including the adopted strategic plan document.

Please provide records in electronic format (native files, including spreadsheets where maintained, or searchable PDF) where available, and produce records on a rolling basis as they are located and reviewed, beginning with the tabulation, scoring records, and executed contract, rather than holding all records until the full set is complete. If a responsive record is held by a third-party portal or vendor on the District's behalf, please produce it or identify where it is publicly posted. If any portion of a record is withheld or redacted, please cite the specific statutory exception relied upon and release all reasonably segregable portions. If fees are expected to exceed $50, please contact me with an itemized estimate before processing so I may narrow the request; I do not authorize fees above $50 without my prior written approval.

Thank you.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Felipe Acano

title: Third-Party-Owned Flock Hardware (Savannah City Clerk)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Third-Party-Owned Flock Hardware (Savannah City Clerk)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any contract, master services agreement, memorandum of understanding or agreement, interlocal or intergovernmental agreement, grant agreement, nondisclosure agreement, or similar document between the Savannah Police Department and any of the following that concerns Flock Safety cameras, solar panels, mounting or power equipment, or other Flock hardware: (a) the Savannah Area Regional Intelligence Center (SARIC); (b) the Georgia Information Sharing and Analysis Center (GISAC); (c) any High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) program; (d) the Georgia Bureau of Investigation or any other regional intelligence center, fusion center, or task force; or (e) any agency, institution, or private party other than the City of Savannah and Flock Safety.
Existing records, such as asset inventories, purchase orders, invoices, grant award documents, installation or deployment records, or hardware lists from the Department's Flock account, sufficient to identify any Flock camera, solar panel, or other Flock hardware used by the Department that is owned, funded, leased, or installed by an entity other than the City of Savannah, including that entity's name.

This request includes responsive records that Flock Safety or another private contractor maintains on the City's behalf. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B). If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and produce all reasonably segregable portions.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

title: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any University Place School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

title: Deaths-in-custody

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Deaths-in-custody
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Ohio Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant to federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organization of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

Dear Records Coordinator,

I am following up on our Massachusetts Public Records Law request of September 23, 2026 (MuckRock request #221677) for records about 19 Rawson Rd, Hanover, MA 02339 (Smokeeter Sales & Svc and Air Cleaning Services LLC). On September 23 the Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection (MassDEP) records manager forwarded the request to the Southeastern Regional Office (SERO), which would follow up directly.

Since then, the Bureau of Waste Site Cleanup (BWSC) in Boston replied on September 24 and the Bureau of Air and Waste (BAW) in Boston on October 1 that they have no records. We have not yet heard from SERO.

Thank you for the list of public sources in MassDEP's September 24 email. We have searched most of them. The online Waste Site portal and the MassDEP underground storage tank database list nothing at this address. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) lists hazardous waste ID MAR000595850 (Air Cleaning Services LLC), with no inspections recorded. The Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs (EEA) Data Portal and the EEA ePLACE permit portal list no facility, permit, inspection or enforcement records at this address. These sources list records but do not hold the documents themselves.

Could you please let us know the status of SERO's search and when we can expect a response? We are still asking for the hazardous waste file for MAR000595850 and any earlier handler at this address, industrial wastewater and floor-drain records, and spill records.

Thank you,

Vlad Gaylun

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: (WA ESD 171) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com)
exchanged with any district email account, alias, or internal
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient,
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's
available archival retention window.

TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals,
and generalized policy or administrative discussions.

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions
may be withheld.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5)
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

title: Flock Safety System Usage and Cost Information (Denton Police Department)

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Flock Safety System Usage and Cost Information (Denton Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Audit logs dating back to January 1, 2026 for searches of any part of the Flock Safety system dating from the initial contract by government employees, private entities operating on behalf of the government, and/or unauthorized searches of the system by any party.

2. Official policy documents that show when and how the Flock Safety system may and/or may not be used.

3. Records of all alleged occurances of nonpermissible searches of Flock Safety systems to include the search criteria, the system(s) searched, the name of the individual that made the search, the stated reason(s) for the search, the current employment status of the one(s) alleged to have misused the system, and a copy of all disciplinary proceedings and the disposition of such proceedings that occurred as a result of the alleged misuse of the system.

4. A list of all criminal charges filed on or after January 1, 2026 where the data from Flock Safety has been admitted into evidence. This list need only include the venue for the case, the docket number, the associated law enforcement agency, the agency's case number(s) associated with the charges, the date the case was filed,  and the disposition status of the case (if available).

5. Financial records that disclose the amount of money disbursed to Flock Safety, Inc. since January 1, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. Given the volume of this records request, I would prefer the request filled electronically by USB flash drive if available, or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nicholas Squires

communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

## PRESERVATION DEMAND ##

Pursuant to O'Neill v. City of Shoreline, 170 Wn.2d 138 (2010), and WAC 44-14-03005, your agency's obligation to preserve all records responsive to this request attaches upon receipt.

Please immediately:

1. Suspend any automated deletion, overwrite, or purge process that would destroy records falling within the scope of this request, whether operating on your agency's own infrastructure or on vendor-managed infrastructure over which your agency holds a contractual right of access or retrieval.

2. Issue a written instruction to your ALPR vendor(s) directing them to halt any automated deletion of records within the scope of this request pending its resolution.

## VENDOR-HELD RECORDS ##

In Rodriguez v. City of Stanwood & Sedro-Woolley (Skagit County Superior Court, No. 22-2-00477-29, Nov. 6, 2025), the court held that ALPR data held by a third-party SaaS vendor on behalf of a government agency is a public record subject to PRA disclosure, and that vendor custody does not relieve the agency of its production obligation. That ruling is currently on appeal to the Washington Court of Appeals, Division 1; the appeal does not stay the disclosure obligation.  Each request below that encompasses vendor-held records is made on this basis. Please retrieve and produce all responsive records held by your ALPR vendor(s) on your agency's behalf.

## ELECTRONIC REPRODUCTION AND THE DUTY TO PRODUCE ##

I seek existing records only. I understand that no agency is required to create a new record in response to a PRA request. However, producing a screenshot or other faithful reproduction of an existing electronic display is not creating a new record — it is reproducing an existing one, in the same manner as photocopying or scanning a paper document. Where a requested record exists only as a display within a software interface, a screenshot or faithful reproduction of that display, or an export of that display to any available file format (including CSV, PDF, or JSON), is an acceptable and required form of production.

## FEE REQUEST ##

I am requesting these records for research and public interest purposes, submitted through MuckRock, a nonprofit journalism platform. I request that your agency consider waiving any fees given that this request is submitted for research and public interest purposes and that electronic production of the requested records should entail minimal or no actual cost under RCW 42.56.120. For any anticipated costs, please notify me before incurring them so that I may prioritize or narrow the request. This notification requirement should not be construed as authorization to delay production of records for which no fee will be incurred pending resolution of fees for other records in this request

## RECORDS REQUESTED ##

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All existing ALPR scan records (e.g., stored in your agency's ALPR system or any system used to store, process, or query ALPR data, such as Axon Evidence.com, Flock Safety portal, or Motorola/Vigilant), including all metadata fields associated with each record as captured and stored by the system. This includes but is not limited to: license plate number, timestamp, GPS coordinates, camera or device identifier, lane identifier, direction of travel, confidence score, vehicle make, vehicle model, vehicle color, image file metadata, and any field capturing information about vehicle occupants or associated individuals.

2. All system audit logs associated with the records in item 1, as natively maintained in your agency's systems or your vendor's systems, reflecting every query performed against your agency's ALPR system, including for each query: the date and time, the user identifier or badge number of the querying user, the Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) of the querying agency, and the entry in the "reason for search," "justification," "purpose," or equivalent field. Where no justification was entered for a query, the log entry reflecting that absence is itself a responsive record and should be produced.

To facilitate partial rolling production while the full dataset is being compiled, please prioritize production of records associated with the following specific license plates. Prioritizing these plates does not limit or waive any part of this request:

	Seattle Police Department specialized and long-service fleet vehicles
	(from City of Seattle fleet records; plates may have been re-registered
	but vehicles are believed to remain in service):
	c. 50816D  — Surveillance trailer (Skywatch Sentinel, 2010)
	d. 50887D  — Hybrid command center (2007, est. replacement 2031)
	e. 54180D  — Police armored vehicle (2011, est. replacement 2031)
	f. 43500D  — Bomb squad trailer (2005)
	g. 26073D  — Bomb containment vessel trailer (1997)
	h. 41461D  — Communications van (2005)
	i. 44372D  — Command vehicle (2005)
	j. 54148D  — Riot fencing trailer (2011)
	k. 54362D  — CSI van with generator (2012)
	l. 50295D  — SWAT cutaway van (2008)
	m. 54117D  — CSI van (2011)
	n. 24208D  — Weapons vehicle (1987)
	
	Washington State fleet vehicles (by plate pattern):
	o. All plates with the prefix or suffix "WSP"
	p. All plates with the prefix "XMT"
	
	Other:
	a. BCH-478
	b. 826-ZVA

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Phil Mocek

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #P009776-032926
communications.communication:
Dear Mount Vernon Police Records Division,

This responds to your April 1, 2026 message requesting clarification.

## Regarding bona fide researcher status ##

RCW 42.56.080 authorizes any person to inspect or copy public records without identification or proof of any qualification. No such showing is required to make a PRA request.

To the extent your letter invokes ESSB 6002, the bona fide researcher provision appears in Section 5(5) and applies only to "automated license plate reader data" as defined in Section 2(3). Audit trail data is separately defined in Section 2(2) and is expressly stated to "not include automated license plate reader data." The researcher limitation does not apply to the audit trail data requested in item 2 of the original request. If the Department intends to deny any portion of this request under any exemption, please provide a written statement identifying the exemption and the specific records to which it applies, as required by RCW 42.56.210.

## Regarding clarification of "system audit logs" ##

The request sought records corresponding to what ESSB 6002 Section 2(2) defines as "audit trail data": all data collected or generated by an automated license plate reader system that identifies how the system is accessed or used, including information about who accesses or uses the system and how and when it is accessed or used. ESSB 6002 Section 8(1) requires agencies to retain this data for two years and specifies that it must include, at minimum:

 (a) the identity or username of the person who accessed or queried the system, and the organization or entity with which that person is affiliated;
 (b) the date and time of access or search;
 (c) the data elements used to query the system;
 (d) the stated purpose for access, including offense type for criminal investigations;
 (e) any associated call for service or case number; and
 (f) the location of the cameras accessed.

The request is for all records your agency maintains that serve this function, in whatever format they are maintained. If your agency stores this data under a different label or in a different system (including any records held by or retrievable from your ALPR vendor), please produce whatever records you maintain that reflect ALPR system access and use.

Cordially,
Phil Mocek

communications.subject: E: P009776-032926 --- Timely Clarification Provided; Request Not Abandoned
communications.communication:
RE: Public Records Request Reference # P009776-032926

Dear Mount Vernon Police Records Division,

I write to dispute the abandonment declaration in your May 1, 2026 letter.

Your April 1, 2026, message requested clarification within thirty days. Today, May 1, 2026, is the thirtieth day. I provided the requested clarification today via MuckRock — the platform through which this request was submitted and through which all prior communications have occurred — before receiving your abandonment notice. The clarification was timely. The request is not abandoned and I do not withdraw it.

I request that you reopen this request and process the clarification I submitted today.

Additionally, I note that your April 1 letter requested "proof of bona fide researcher status." RCW 42.56.080 authorizes any person to request public records without identifying themselves, stating a purpose, or demonstrating any qualification. No such proof is required or lawfully demandable as a condition of processing a PRA request. To the extent your letter invoked ESSB 6002 Section 5(5), that provision applies only to "automated license plate reader data" as defined in Section 2(3); audit trail data is separately defined in Section 2(2) as explicitly excluding ALPR data, and the researcher limitation in Section 5(5) does not apply to it.

Your letter states that "the one-year statute of limitations to seek judicial review has started to run." I dispute the premise. The limitations period under RCW 42.56.550 runs from an agency's failure to comply with the Act. A purported abandonment based on an untimely clarification demand — or a clarification demand that was itself not authorized by statute — does not constitute a lawful denial and does not trigger the limitations period. I am preserving all rights.

Cordially,
Phil Mocek
-- 
Phil Mocek
207684-97812171@requests.muckrock.com

communications.subject: [Records Center] Public Safety Records Request :: P009776-032926
communications.communication:
--- Please respond above this line --- 

Mr. Mocek, 
In your request dated March 29, 2026 (Public Safety Records Request #P009776) you requested "ALPR scan records" and "system audit logs," indicated that your request was for "research and public interest purposes," and asked for a waiver of fees. 
Because your response was received on May 1, 2026, your request is reopened. 
As you indicated in your response dated May 1, 2026, it appears that you are aware that the "ALPR data" (the "scan records") you requested is exempt from disclosure under the Public Records Act absent evidence that the request is for research as defined in RCW 42.48.010. Because unauthorized disclosure of ALPR data is a crime, the City properly requested that you provide evidence that you qualified as a researcher as defined in RCW 42.48.010. The City also requested clarification of what you meant by "system audit logs." ESSB 6002, Washington's Driver's Safety Act, which was signed and went into effect on March 31, 2026, does not include the word "logs" or "logs," and the records staff thought it best to ask you to clarify what records your request intended to cover. From your May 1, 2026, response, it's now clear that you sought "audit trail data." 
As I believe your May 1, 2026, response indicates, you are aware that ALPR data ("ALPR scan records") is exempt from disclosure under the Public Records Act. ESSB 6002 Sec. 4 plainly and clearly provides that ALPR data “shall not be used or shared for any other purpose" than the uses set out in sec. 3(2): (a) comparing ALPR data with specific databases, (b) searches for stolen vehicles, (c) missing or endangered persons, (d) registered to a person with an outstanding felony or gross misdemeanor warrant, (e) looking for a vehicle involved in a felony or gross misdemeanor. (f) etc. ESSB Sec. 5 further provides that “Automated license plate reader data is not subject to disclosure under the public records act, chapter 42.56 RCW, except such data may be used for bona fide research. . .” The law prohibits the use or sharing of collected ALPR data for purposes other than those specified uses and requires that APLR data be deleted after 21 days unless “retained pursuant to a valid, court-issued, probable cause felony or gross misdemeanor warrant or subpoena, or as permitted by court order in criminal or civil cases.” Absent a court-issued order and as you have not submitted any proof that you are a researcher as defined in RCW 42.48.010, the City cannot disclose the requested ALPR data or hold it beyond 21 days without committing a crime. See Sec. 10 of ESSB 6002. 
However, the audit trail data ("system audit logs") you requested is not exempt from disclosure and will be disclosed to you after any "unique identifiers" have been deleted from the audit trail data. See Sec. 8, ESSB 6002. The City expects to complete the review of its audit trail data by May 22nd, 2026. 
The City's Policy and Procedures for PRA requests allows the waiver of fees for requests made by a state or local agency and when the costs of copying totals less than two dollars. An estimate of your fees, if any will be due, will be provided shortly. 
If you meant to request something other than "APLR data" and "audit trail data" as those terms are used in Washington's Driver's Privacy Act, please further clarify your request. If you have any questions about the reopening of your request, the disclosure of ALPR data and ALPR audit trails, please let me know. 
Sincerely, 
Mount Vernon Police Records Division

RE: PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST of March 29, 2026, Reference # P009776-032926 

Dear Phil Mocek, 

The Mount Vernon Police Department received a public records request from you on March 29, 2026. You requested the following: 
"To Whom It May Concern: 

## PRESERVATION DEMAND ## 

Pursuant to O'Neill v. City of Shoreline, 170 Wn.2d 138 (2010), and WAC 44-14-03005, your agency's obligation to preserve all records responsive to this request attaches upon receipt. 

Please immediately: 

1. Suspend any automated deletion, overwrite, or purge process that would destroy records falling within the scope of this request, whether operating on your agency's own infrastructure or on vendor-managed infrastructure over which your agency holds a contractual right of access or retrieval. 

2. Issue a written instruction to your ALPR vendor(s) directing them to halt any automated deletion of records within the scope of this request pending its resolution. 

## VENDOR-HELD RECORDS ## 

In Rodriguez v. City of Stanwood & Sedro-Woolley (Skagit County Superior Court, No. 22-2-00477-29, Nov. 6, 2025), the court held that ALPR data held by a third-party SaaS vendor on behalf of a government agency is a public record subject to PRA disclosure, and that vendor custody does not relieve the agency of its production obligation. That ruling is currently on appeal to the Washington Court of Appeals, Division 1; the appeal does not stay the disclosure obligation. Each request below that encompasses vendor-held records is made on this basis. Please retrieve and produce all responsive records held by your ALPR vendor(s) on your agency's behalf. 

## ELECTRONIC REPRODUCTION AND THE DUTY TO PRODUCE ## 

I seek existing records only. I understand that no agency is required to create a new record in response to a PRA request. However, producing a screenshot or other faithful reproduction of an existing electronic display is not creating a new record — it is reproducing an existing one, in the same manner as photocopying or scanning a paper document. Where a requested record exists only as a display within a software interface, a screenshot or faithful reproduction of that display, or an export of that display to any available file format (including CSV, PDF, or JSON), is an acceptable and required form of production. 

## FEE REQUEST ## 

I am requesting these records for research and public interest purposes, submitted through MuckRock, a nonprofit journalism platform. I request that your agency consider waiving any fees given that this request is submitted for research and public interest purposes and that electronic production of the requested records should entail minimal or no actual cost under RCW 42.56.120. For any anticipated costs, please notify me before incurring them so that I may prioritize or narrow the request. This notification requirement should not be construed as authorization to delay production of records for which no fee will be incurred pending resolution of fees for other records in this request 

## RECORDS REQUESTED ## 

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records: 

1. All existing ALPR scan records (e.g., stored in your agency's ALPR system or any system used to store, process, or query ALPR data, such as Axon Evidence.com, Flock Safety portal, or Motorola/Vigilant), including all metadata fields associated with each record as captured and stored by the system. This includes but is not limited to: license plate number, timestamp, GPS coordinates, camera or device identifier, lane identifier, direction of travel, confidence score, vehicle make, vehicle model, vehicle color, image file metadata, and any field capturing information about vehicle occupants or associated individuals. 

2. All system audit logs associated with the records in item 1, as natively maintained in your agency's systems or your vendor's systems, reflecting every query performed against your agency's ALPR system, including for each query: the date and time, the user identifier or badge number of the querying user, the Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) of the querying agency, and the entry in the "reason for search," "justification," "purpose," or equivalent field. Where no justification was entered for a query, the log entry reflecting that absence is itself a responsive record and should be produced. 

To facilitate partial rolling production while the full dataset is being compiled, please prioritize production of records associated with the following specific license plates. Prioritizing these plates does not limit or waive any part of this request: 

Seattle Police Department specialized and long-service fleet vehicles 
(from City of Seattle fleet records; plates may have been re-registered 
but vehicles are believed to remain in service): 
c. 50816D — Surveillance trailer (Skywatch Sentinel, 2010) 
d. 50887D — Hybrid command center (2007, est. replacement 2031) 
e. 54180D — Police armored vehicle (2011, est. replacement 2031) 
f. 43500D — Bomb squad trailer (2005) 
g. 26073D — Bomb containment vessel trailer (1997) 
h. 41461D — Communications van (2005) 
i. 44372D — Command vehicle (2005) 
j. 54148D — Riot fencing trailer (2011) 
k. 54362D — CSI van with generator (2012) 
l. 50295D — SWAT cutaway van (2008) 
m. 54117D — CSI van (2011) 
n. 24208D — Weapons vehicle (1987) 

Washington State fleet vehicles (by plate pattern): 
o. All plates with the prefix or suffix "WSP" 
p. All plates with the prefix "XMT" 

Other: 
a. BCH-478 
b. 826-ZVA 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Phil Mocek

___________________________________________________________________
Also note that after a thorough review of our files, the Salem Police Department's Records Office has identified an email responsive to your request. However, we are unable to release this record, as it is legally exempt from mandatory public disclosure.
Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law<https://www.mass.gov/files/2017-06/Public%20Records%20Law.pdf>, G.L. c. 4, § 7(26)<https://www.mass.gov/info-details/exemptions>, the requested email is being withheld in its entirety under the following legal protections:
Basis for Exemption

  *
Common Law Attorney-Client Privilege: Under established Massachusetts common law, confidential communications between a governmental entity and its legal counsel are strictly protected from disclosure to ensure the public entity can obtain candid, reliable legal advice. See Suffolk Construction Co. v. Division of Capital Asset Management, 449 Mass. 444 (2007). The withheld email (dated 8-24-26) is that of the Chief of Police Lucas Miller. This email consists of pre-decisional protocol and policy questions aimed at establishing compliance frameworks. Release of this preliminary, deliberative information would stifle the free, honest exchange of ideas required for law enforcement agencies to successfully navigate new regulatory requirements.

Due to the fact that the entire substance of the communication consists of a request for legal consultation and ongoing policy formulation, there are no segregable, purely factual portions that can be redacted and released.
No additional responsive records were located in the custody or control of this office.

communications.communication:
Hi,
I am responding to your request below:
 Pursuant to your October 23, 2026 public records request copied below, in regards to Portions #1 and #2 of your request, in an effort of transparency policies and procedures for the Brookline Police Department are available to the public at all times; no PRRs are needed to view any of these materials. Please see the following link for full list of Department policies and procedures:
https://www.brooklinepolice.com/185/Brookline-Police-Policies-and-Procedures<https://protect-us.mimecast.com/s/K-XBCOY58ku06L7wiESm_X?domain=brooklinepolice.com>
In regards to portion #3 in the attached PRR; The mandatory disclosure provision of the Public Records Law only applies to information that is in the custody of the Department at the time the request is received. As a result, there is no obligation for a department to create a record for a requester to honor a request. See G.L. c. 4, section 7(26) (defining "public records" as materials which have already been "made or received" by a public entity); see also 32 Op. Attorney Gen. 157, 165 (May 18, 1977) (custodian is not obliged to create a record in response to a request for information); see also A Guide to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Division of Public Records, p. 7 (January 2013) (hereinafter Public Records Guide). As such the Department has no materials to release.
 There are no fees associated with this request.  At this time the Department considers this request closed.
 You have the right to appeal this determination to the supervisor of records pursuant to G.L. c.66, § 10A(a) and the right to seek judicial review of an unfavorable decision by commencing a civil action in superior court under G.L. c.66, §10A(c).  Any and all appeals should be filed through the Sec of the Commonwealth.
 Signed,
Amanda Williams
Records Clerk
Brookline Police Department

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 9/1/2021 to 10/1/2021. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2021) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman
